title: Lift & Anchor: Conversion Canvas for Dedicated → Private Upgrades + SLA Bundles
body:
Purpose:
This working canvas is an operational playbook for CS/AMs to run targeted conversion motions for customers on Dedicated who are candidates for Private deployments or premium SLA bundles. It focuses on a short, high-touch sprint (4–8 weeks) to: 1) surface technical blockers, 2) quantify commercial value, 3) stage a low-effort technical validation, and 4) close to a conversion or clear next-step.

High-level principles:
- Move fast: short, measurable sprints, avoid open-ended evaluation timelines.
- De-risk technically first: validate networking, perf, and security gating early.
- Make economics obvious: estimate token/cost delta and show TCO 12/24 month impact.
- Use modular offers: separate Dedicated→Private pilot, then SLA add-on as an attach.

Who this playbook is for:
- AMs and CSMs handling mid-market and enterprise accounts on Dedicated with predictable spend patterns and regulatory needs.
- Solutions engineers and cloud architects who will perform the technical proof-of-concept (PoC).

Triggers to run this play:
- Annual renewal within 6–9 months and customer has inflection in usage >30% QoQ.
- Customer requests VPC networking, audit logs, or dedicated tenancy for compliance.
- Region latency SLAs or data residency requests that Dedicated cannot meet.
- Pricing is causing cross-sell limit — customer asking for private tenancy or lower egress/compute cost.

Sprint timeline (recommended 6 weeks):
Week 0 (Prep): internal alignment, baseline metrics, legal redlines check.
Week 1: Customer kickoff — clarify drivers, KPIs, and define success.
Week 2: Technical discovery + run lightweight compatibility checklist.
Week 3: Pilot design — propose 2-week pilot (Private in lab or VPC staging) or SLA trial.
Week 4–5: Pilot execution — SRE/SE monitor, collect perf and cost deltas.
Week 6: Commercial proposal + close or defined next-steps.

Core artifacts to produce during sprint (deliverables):
- One-pager: "Why Private / SLA bundle for <customer>" (tech + econ bullets)
- Pilot runbook: objectives, success metrics, rollback plan, contact matrix
- Econ appendix: estimated unit cost comparison (Dedicated vs Private + SLA) and 12-month TCO tables
- Proposal deck: 6 slides for decision-makers (summary, findings, pilot results, price options, legal terms, next steps)

Technical qualification checklist (to be completed by SE fast):
- Network: VPN/VPC peering feasibility, IP requirements, bandwidth estimate, firewall rules
- Data: Encryption at rest/transport checks, KMS integration feasibility, data residency constraints
- Model compatibility: quantization/profile compatibility, sequence length expected, KV cache sizing
- Ops: Logging/trace ingestion, retention needs, monitoring endpoints, alerting hooks
- Capacity: projected peak RPS, sustained throughput, autoscaling policy constraints
- Compliance: gap vs customer controls matrix (SOC2/GDPR/ISO/PCI as applicable)

Pilot design templates (pick 1):
- VPC staging pilot (recommended): provision a mirrored Private environment in a non-prod VPC, run 2 representative workloads for 72 hours under peak traffic profile. Success if latency within SLO +/- 15% and cost delta within expected range.
- SLA trial: enable premium SLA for 30 days on a subset of routes, capture uptime and incident response metrics. Success if no infra-level incidents and support turnaround within contracted windows.
- Hybrid run: leave traffic on Dedicated but route burst to Private for high-load periods; measure failover performance.

Customer conversation scripts (concise):
1) Kickoff (email):
Subject: Pilot proposal — Private deployment + SLA trial for <product/team>
Hi <Name>,
Based on our recent discussions about compliance and predictable latency, we propose a short pilot to validate Private deployment and our premium SLA. The goal: prove performance and estimate TCO impact so your procurement can make a clear decision. Proposed timeline: 6 weeks. Can we set a 30-minute kickoff this week?
Thanks,
<Jenna/AM>

2) Mid-pilot check-in (slack/email):
Quick update — pilot running, observed p95 latency down 13% on route X, KV hit-rate looks stable. Next 48h we’ll run load spike to verify autoscale behavior. Flag any concerns.

3) Close/Proposal (email):
Subject: Pilot results & recommended next steps
Hi <Name>,
Thanks for running the pilot. Summary: performance met SLOs, there were 2 config items we fixed, and estimated 12-mo TCO delta is +$X with projected unit cost savings on high-volume routes. Attached is a compact proposal with 2 commercial options: a 12-mo Private commit (with optional elevated SLA) and a 24-mo discounted commit that includes onboarding credits. Happy to review live.
Best,
<Jenna/AM>

Commercial offer constructs (sample options):
- Option A: 12-month Private commit (baseline price) + standard onboarding (4 days) + optional SLA at +10% of committed monthly fee.
- Option B: 24-month Private commit with 15% discount on monthly committed capacity + SLA included for first 12 months.
- Option C: Dedicated retention + burst-to-private for high spikes (no full migration) — lower upfront cost, SLA as add-on.

How to price the SLA add-on (rules of thumb):
- Base SLA add-on = 8–12% of committed monthly invoice for typical enterprise accounts.
- Higher-criticality customers (financial/healthcare) = 12–18% due to faster response and expanded runbooks.
- Offer an "incident escrow" credit for first 3 months to reduce perceived risk.

Decision-makers and influencers to map:
- Technical: SRE/Infra lead, Security/Compliance officer, Platform architect
- Economic: Procurement, FinOps, VP Product/Engineering
- Executive champion: VP/Head who owns ML or product roadmap and cares about reliability or data residency

Escalation map (if stall):
1) AM & SE re-engage with fresh econ modeling and proposed concession (e.g., onboarding credit).
2) Solutions Eng leadership offers signature-level technical call.
3) Director of CS or commercial lead offers a short-term discounted pilot or extended payment terms.

Risk register (common blockers & mitigations):
- Blocker: Security review timeline extends beyond sprint. Mitigation: pre-populate security artifact pack and run a 1:1 with security reviewer in week 1.
- Blocker: Network peering blocked by corporate infra. Mitigation: propose a managed transit path and temporary secure proxy for pilot.
- Blocker: Unexpected cost delta. Mitigation: commit to a 30-day cost review and propose a capped delta concession for pilot period.

QBR slide outline (6 slides):
1) Executive summary (ask + one-line why)
2) Business drivers & KPIs (cost, latency, reliability)
3) Pilot design & timeline
4) Results & technical findings (metrics, logs summary)
5) Commercial options & recommended path
6) Next steps & decision calendar

KPIs to measure success:
- Time to first meaningful result (days)
- p95 latency delta between Dedicated and Private (ms and %)
quick_actions: Request security artifact pack: security@redwood.com (include SOC2, encryption notes, KMS flow)
Open JIRA ticket for pilot infra provisioning with tag 'private-pilot'
Schedule 30-min exec alignment within 2 weeks of pilot completion
